title: Extension by zero through the schematic closure
statement:
In the situation of [det-nagata-density-normalization-setup], let
$\Lambda$ be a condensed coefficient ring with pulled-back coefficient
sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Z,\Lambda_{\overline X}$. For every sheaf $M$ of
$\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}$ the unit
$\eta:j_!M\to i_*i^*j_!M$ of $i^*\dashv i_*$ is an isomorphism, and the
base-change isomorphism $i^*j_!M\simeq j_{Z,!}M$ identifies it with a natural
isomorphism

$$
j_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }i_*j_{Z,!}M .
$$

Consequently, for every complex $K$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules (unbounded), the
same map, applied degreewise, is an isomorphism of complexes
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$, and it induces the identification
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$ in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$.

proof.text: The setup gives $\overline X$ and $Z$ qcqs, $V$ an open with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$, and $j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ a quasi-compact open immersion. Quasi-compactness of the morphisms $j_V$ and $j$ is checked as follows. For an affine open $A\subseteq\overline X$, [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies $j_V^{-1}(A)$ and $j^{-1}(A)$ with the open subsets $V\cap A$ and $j(X)\cap A$ of the Noetherian scheme $\overline X$; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes these opens quasi-compact, and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] then gives that $j_V$ and $j$ are quasi-compact. We read “condensed coefficient ring” in the module-object statement in the commutative sense required by [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star] and [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]; this is the standing coefficient convention and adds no geometric hypothesis.

source.place: Step 1: geometric quasi-compactness and the retained coefficient convention

proof.text: For $T\in\{X,Z,V,\overline X\}$ choose the small skeleton and coefficient universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The monoidally stable local equivalences needed by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] are supplied by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso](2), for abelian presheaves; [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] supplies the sheaf tensor and strong monoidal sheafification. The pulled-back coefficient object is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Thus the canonical internal/sectionwise equivalence applies. In particular the internal module category is abelian, since its equivalence with the abelian category of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is additive and exact by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport].

source.place: Step 1: hypotheses for the internal/sectionwise equivalence

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] to $j,j_Z,j_V,i$ with the coefficient isomorphisms $\alpha_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. It identifies the internal operations with sectionwise operations and their actual units. Clauses (1) and (2) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf], for $(j_V,i)$ and for $j$ and $j_Z$ with their closed complements, give exact $i_*,j_!,j_{Z,!}$. Its clause (3) then gives the internal-module exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_{V,!}j_V^*N\longrightarrow N\xrightarrow{\eta_N}i_*i^*N\longrightarrow0.$$
The map $\eta_N$ is the specified unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$, by the unit compatibility in the transport lemma. Exactness of $i^*$ follows from [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits](2) by the same transport.

source.place: Step 1: transport of the exact operations and the localization unit

proof.text: The square with top arrow $\mathrm{id}_X$, bottom arrow $i:Z\to\overline X$, and vertical arrows $j_Z,j$ is cartesian by setup clause (3). In the sectionwise module category, clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives $i^*j_!\cong j_{Z,!}$ because $Z$ is qcqs. The operation and adjunction compatibility of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] carries this canonical base-change transformation to the internal-module pullback and internal extensions by zero. Hence the resulting canonical isomorphism is the module isomorphism $\beta_M:i^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{Z,!}M$, natural in $M$.

The setup gives $X\times_{\overline X}V=\varnothing$, and $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], hence qcqs as in the setup. Apply clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] to $g=j_V$ and the open immersion $j$. The pullback open is the empty scheme, so the sectionwise extension by zero is the zero module sheaf. Through the operation comparisons of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], this identifies the actual internal pullback $j_V^*j_!M$ with the zero internal module.

Apply the internal-module exact sequence from Step 3 to $N=j_!M$. Step 5 makes its first term zero, so $0\to j_!M\xrightarrow{\eta_M}i_*i^*j_!M\to0$. The category of sectionwise module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is abelian, and the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] makes the internal category $\Mod_{\Lambda_{\overline X}}$ abelian with exact sequences corresponding (an equivalence of additive categories preserves kernels and cokernels); hence this unit is a monomorphism and an epimorphism in an abelian category, i.e. an isomorphism. It is the specified unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$ by the identification in Step 3, rather than a unit from a different sectionwise adjunction. Composing it with $i_*\beta_M$ gives the required natural isomorphism $j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*j_{Z,!}M$.

For an arbitrary integer-indexed complex $K$, apply the natural isomorphism $\theta=i_*\beta\circ\eta$ in each degree. Naturality gives $\theta_{K^{n+1}}j_!(d^n)=i_*j_{Z,!}(d^n)\theta_{K^n}$; composing with inverse components shows that the inverses also commute with differentials. This is an isomorphism of complexes. By exactness from Step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] applies to each of $j_!,j_{Z,!},i_*$ on the abelian module categories, with no boundedness assumption. These termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the chain natural isomorphism to the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], giving exactly $j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$ in the asserted unbounded derived category.

Step checks: Step 1 gets quasi-compactness of j_V and j from Noetherian opens (for j it is already part of def-nagata-compactification). Step 2 checks every hypothesis of the internal/sectionwise equivalence: small site, local-iso clause (2), sheaf tensor, commutative Λ_T. Step 3 meets the hypotheses of det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf clauses (1)-(3) for (j_V,i) on qcqs X̄, for j, and for j_Z on qcqs Z; exactness of i^* comes from det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits(2). Step 6: the unit is mono and epi in an abelian category, and it is the specified unit. Step 7 uses exact-functor derived factorization and localization (2), with no boundedness assumption. The new node lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport is true: the internal and sectionwise inverse image, direct image, adjunction, open shriek (both have underlying sheaf j^Ab_! and are left adjoint to the same restriction) and base-change mates all correspond.
